findings.title: A word hint is given the whole answer typed so far, which a secret prompt copies into strings that cannot be wiped
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Low: needs access to the process memory; the typed answer itself becomes a string once it is read.
findings.reproduction: docs/audits/AUD-019-harnesses/probes.ts, first case: the public phrase abandon … about is typed key by key into readLine with the production BIP39 hints, wrapped to count the words of each text a hint is given.
findings.expected: The hint needs the word being typed and enough of the words before it to tell the form of the line; SECURITY.md: temporary copies of the phrase data are cleared as far as possible.
findings.observed: typedBefore decoded line.subarray(0, cursor): each redraw built a string of the whole answer so far, up to all 12 words; the probe fails with 12 > 4.
findings.impact: While a seed phrase is typed on the private screen, every pause leaves another copy of the words typed so far in the heap until the memory is reused: a few dozen strings for a 24-word phrase. Core dumps are off, so reading them needs access to the process memory, swap or a hibernation image.
findings.recommendedFix: Give the hint only the word being typed and a few before it (a named constant), decoded from the buffer that readLine owns and wipes; add the probe as a regression test.
findings.requiredVerification: The probe's first case passes; the word-hint and terminal tests and verify-terminal-input.py still pass.

findings.title: Core-dump calls and the claim of a probed boundary are written in more than one place
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Low: both copies behave the same today; the risk is a later change to one of them.
findings.reproduction: node scripts/verify-no-copies.mjs --tokens 35: src/cli/sandbox-linux.ts:343-350 = src/cli/sandbox-macos.ts:170-177 (39 tokens). Reading protection.ts beside sandbox-linux.ts and sandbox-macos.ts: both open the same C library by its own literal name, and protection.ts keeps setrlimit and prctl apart from the sandbox of its system.
findings.expected: AGENTS.md, no repetition: a rule, constant or library name has one source; a protection of a system belongs to that system's type (delegation).
findings.observed: The code that records a probe's result as held, broken or unknown is written twice; RLIMIT_CORE, the struct rlimit size and the C library names appear in protection.ts and in the sandbox modules; protection.ts decides by platform whether core dumps exist, which the sandbox of that platform knows.
findings.impact: A change to the rule of one platform, such as how a failed probe is reported, can miss the other copy, and a new system needs edits in protection.ts as well as its own module.
findings.recommendedFix: One SandboxRecord type for held boundaries and their reasons, with claim and reach; core dumps switched off and read back by each system's sandbox in start(), asked through coreDumps(); protection.ts asks the sandbox instead of keeping its own calls.
findings.requiredVerification: The 35-token scan finds no sandbox copy; the sandbox and protection tests, the executable check and the CLI self-test pass; a protected process without node:ffi still refuses a secret.

findings.title: The changelog and the release notes still describe share cards in every form, which the card redesign removed
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Low and not blocking for the code; the release text must be corrected before v0.1.0 is published, since it is copied into the release.
affectedFiles: docs/releases/v0.1.0.md, line 33 and its card and secret-handling sections
findings.reproduction: Read CHANGELOG.md line 38 and docs/releases/v0.1.0.md beside src/export/card-codes.ts and the refusal "Shares written as words have no cards"; compare the release notes with the CHANGELOG entries of 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13.
findings.expected: The changelog and the release notes say what the code does; the release notes carry the changes of the release.
findings.observed: Both say that share cards print word numbers, Unicode codes or Bytewords, three to a card, beside random colours; the code refuses cards of shares in words. The release notes also say that separate cards print the size of the set, which they no longer do, and lack the redesign, the word hints, the system sandbox, the wiping of saved documents and QR input, and codes read apart or run together.
findings.impact: A reader of the release expects cards that the program refuses, and does not learn of new protections and inputs.
findings.evidence: Source and document review recorded in this report
findings.recommendedFix: Rewrite the changelog line for cards of colours and Unicode codes only; bring the release notes in line with the changelog.
findings.requiredVerification: The changelog and release notes agree with the code and with each other; pnpm check (Markdown lists) passes.

findings.title: SECURITY.md says that no limit of the operating system applies, though the system sandbox now enforces some
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Low: it understates the protection rather than overstating it.
affectedFiles: SECURITY.md, section on what limits MnemoCode, and the swap warning
findings.reproduction: Read SECURITY.md lines 22-27 beside src/cli/system-sandbox.ts and the executable check "is held by the system's sandbox (kernel: no sockets)".
findings.expected: SECURITY.md describes the limits as they are: where the system enforces some, which differ by system and version, and what stays usable.
findings.observed: "Neither is a limit of the operating system" and "MnemoCode is not a sandbox"; the swap warning does not say that it is left out when all memory is locked.
findings.impact: A reader judges the protection by a wrong description; a person on a system with the sandbox does not learn that descriptors opened before it, such as the terminal, stay usable.
findings.evidence: Source and document review recorded in this report
findings.recommendedFix: Say that MnemoCode is not a complete sandbox, that only the limits the system enforces stop a compromised program from connecting, that they differ by system and version, and that descriptors opened before them stay usable; name the locked-memory case of the swap warning.
findings.requiredVerification: SECURITY.md agrees with system-sandbox.ts and protection.ts; pnpm check passes.

informationalNotes: Observation, fixed with ARC001: the start menu restricted the system sandbox for the widest needs of any command before it starts each command as a process of its own. On macOS a process inherits the sandbox of the process that starts it, and a second profile applied inside it may be refused, so a command could have run under the menu's wider profile only. Found in review, not executed (no macOS host). The menu now gives up node:ffi and file writes of the permission model only, and each command applies its own sandbox.

AUD-011 and AUD-012 link 20 times to the frosted glass sources (src/export/glass-cards.ts, glass-artwork.ts, glass-layout.ts) that the card redesign removed; the links pointed at the reviewed state. Future reports should link a commit-pinned URL.

readme-examples.py runs each command alone, so the two examples that read a file written by a skipped secret-prompt example fail (decode --input-file direct-unicode.txt, decode --qr-file my-palette-qr.png); a harness limit, recorded as in AUD-018.
The 35-token copy diagnostic finds the overload signatures of askOrCancel in src/cli/ask.ts: declarations, not behaviour, as in AUD-018.

The working tree of 2026-10-12 held another agent's README rewording together with later edits in the same paragraphs, and no copy of it survives; the states of AUD-018's baseline and remediation could therefore not be rebuilt as commits of their own. The reviewed source was committed as five commits ending at the reviewed commit; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and test/portable-modules.test.ts match the AUD-018 baseline hashes.
Node.js 26's libuv opens its io_uring rings at start, before MnemoCode runs, so seccomp can refuse io_uring_setup but not io_uring_enter on those rings; recorded in sandbox-linux.ts.
The encode prompt for a seed phrase takes words only; whether it should also take codes is the owner's open question and not a finding.

fixes.change: HINT_CONTEXT_WORDS = 4: typedBefore decodes only from the fourth word before the cursor, enough to tell Bytewords after the codes of another share or English words among codes. A regression test types abandon … about and asserts that no hint sees more than four words.

sandbox-record.ts holds the interface, SandboxRecord (hold, lack, attempt, reach, claim) and switchOffCoreDumps with RLIMIT_CORE; each system's sandbox switches core dumps off in start() and reports them through coreDumps(); protection.ts keeps no system call of its own and refuses a secret when coreDumps() failed. Tests cover the record, claim and a protected process without node:ffi.

The changelog line now names cards of colours and Unicode codes only; the release notes drop the stale lines and carry the redesign, word hints, system sandbox, wiping of saved documents and QR input, entry 5 and codes read apart or run together.

MnemoCode is not a complete sandbox; only the limits the system enforces, which differ by system and version, stop a compromised program from connecting, and descriptors opened before them stay usable; the swap warning is left out when all memory is locked.
